newsitem.title: USA: Union leader hopes Tosco contract rejected.
newsitem.headline: Union leader hopes Tosco contract rejected.

text.p: An Oil,Chemical and Atomic Workers (OCAW) union leader familiar with labor contract talks going on between OCAW and oil refiner Tosco Corp said he hopes the rank and file of the union rejects Tosco's contract.

David Campbell, chief executive of OCAW Local 1-675, which represents a refinery in Los Angeles Tosco will own from next month, said that while top brass at OCAW earlier this week tentatively approved the Tosco contract, the union's rank and file will ultimately decide the contract's fate.
"I'm hoping it gets defeated," Campbell said of the contract, which covers a total of four California refineries.
Tosco Corp's previously announced $2 billion purchase of the four plants from Unocal Corp closes at the end of the month.

The deal includes the Wilmington refinery, where Campbell represents about 370 workers, the nearby refinery in Carson, another in Rodeo east of San Francisco and the last in Santa Maria located between Los Angeles and San Francisco.
Campbell, noting the separate balloting at the four refineries will be end March 31, noted that the possibility of a strike still existed.

"I'm not only concerned about the workers who are getting whacked, but also about the safety of our (remaining) refinery workers and of the surrounding community," Campbell said, noting the job cuts proposed in the tentative agreement were far too deep for comfort.

But he said that a workers rejection need not signal a strike, but rather a return to the negotiating table or declaration of an impasse, which would in effect put off strike-like confrontation until the contract is negotiated within a few years.

He also noted workers might end up accepting the contract based on Tosco's ultimatum that it will close the Rodeo plant and contract out for maintenance work should workers reject the company's 'last best and and final' offer.
"Even if they're going to vote for it, there's no one on this side who likes it," Campbell said.
